95266.text: What is the term for the parts of an airport not directly involved in flight operations, lying outside the airside, starting from the beginning point of the main access road?

95267.text: Which of the following may enter the landside of an airport?
options: Passengers, staff, passengers' relatives, well-wishers and greeters
Only staff with a valid entry pass
Only passengers who have passed security control

95268.text: Which of the following can be given as an example of the landside of an airport?
options: Areas where the check-in counters are located
Beyond the departure passport control checkpoint

95269.text: Under Annex 17, which of the following is correct regarding taking security measures on the landside of an airport?
options: Security measures must also be taken on the landside to reduce the risk of acts of unlawful interference
No security measures are needed on the landside
The landside is the responsibility of the law enforcement authorities only
Having cameras on the landside alone is sufficient
No additional measures are needed since the landside is considered a security restricted area

95270.text: Which of the following can be given as an example of the airside of an airport?
options: The arriving passenger baggage claim area

95271.text: Which of the following is not considered part of a security restricted area?
options: Catering and aircraft cleaning facilities located airside

95272.text: At airports, what are persons subjected to in order to pass from the airside into a security restricted area?
options: They are not subjected to any control

95273.text: Which of the following is correct regarding demarcated areas?
options: They are established so that alternative measures can be applied and are clearly separated from security restricted areas
They are a subdivision of security restricted areas and the same measures apply
They are established only for scheduled commercial flights
They are found only inside the terminal building
They are areas where no security measures are applied at all

95274.text: By what means can demarcated areas be separated from security restricted areas?
options: By physical measures or by patrolling and surveillance
Only with a wall or wire fence

95275.text: What procedures do aviation security measures basically consist of?

95276.text: What is the term for the methods used to detect prohibited articles in order to prevent acts of unlawful interference?

95277.text: The authorisations that can be used to enter the airside of an airport are divided into which two main groups?
options: The boarding passes used by passengers and the airport entry pass used by non-passengers
Apron plate and vehicle identification card

95278.text: Where is it generally checked whether the identity information on passengers' boarding passes has been written correctly?

95279.text: Which of the following is not among the information that must be found on an airport identity card?
options: The name of the issuing organisation or airport
The areas the person is permitted to access

95280.text: Which expression must be present on crew identity cards to distinguish them from other cards?

95281.text: What does the background check that must be carried out before issuing a person an identity card granting unescorted access to security restricted areas cover?
options: Examination of the person's education, employment and criminal records
Examination of the person's medical report
Examination of the person's financial situation
Examination of the person's travel history
Examination of the person's driving licence details

95282.text: What should be done regarding the identity card of a person who fails the background check?
options: Depending on the situation, it must be immediately deactivated or withdrawn and returned to the issuing organisation
It must remain valid for one year
It should continue to be used only for escorted entries
It should remain with the person but the authorised areas should be narrowed
No action needs to be taken

95283.text: What methods are used to check persons' authorisation to enter the areas they wish to access?

95284.text: Which of the following situations causes an increase in risk in electronic access control?
options: The system being used by unauthorised persons, password sharing, or failure to protect information security
The card reader operating too quickly
The doors being designed for more than one person
Visual control also being carried out
The use of a surveillance system

95285.text: In hybrid access control, what is the most important point the security officer at the checkpoint must not forget?
options: That electronic card readers can only verify the validity of authorisations
That electronic card readers also match the person with the card
That visual control is not necessary
That the card's expiry date cannot be read
That escorted entries are automatically approved

95286.text: The data that can be used in biometric access control are specified in which numbered ICAO document?

95287.text: According to the ICAO document, which biometric data are considered unique and specific to a single person?
options: Fingerprints, facial features and iris pattern
Blood type, DNA and dental structure

95288.text: Which of the following is correct regarding short-term temporary identity cards and documents at the airport?
options: These documents do not permit entry into security restricted areas without an escort
These documents allow free entry into security restricted areas
These documents must have different features from airport identity cards
These documents can only be used on the landside
An expiry date is not required for these documents

95289.text: Which of the following is correct regarding authorisation to enter the airport?
options: No uniform or identity badge grants entry authorisation other than airport entry passes and authorisation documents
An airline uniform alone grants entry authorisation
A company identity badge substitutes for an entry pass
A crew uniform exempts from access control
A law enforcement uniform grants entry authorisation to all areas

95290.text: Which of the following is correct regarding the validity of airport entry passes?
options: It is valid only at the airport where it was issued and cannot be used at another airport
It is valid at all airports nationwide
It is valid at all international airports
It is valid at every airport served by the same airline
It is valid at all facilities in the province where the issuing organisation is located

95291.text: In the event of improper use of an entry pass, who bears the responsibility?
options: The card user together with the organisation or institution the staff member belongs to
Only the authority that issued the card
Only the officer at the security checkpoint

95292.text: Which of the following is not among the situations requiring the immediate return of an airport entry pass to the issuing organisation?
options: The staff member going on annual leave
Expiry of the card's validity period

95293.text: In Turkey, an All Airports Entry Pass is issued to personnel working at a minimum of how many airports?

95294.text: In Turkey, what is the administrative fine applied for 2024 in the event of improper use of an airport entry pass?

95295.text: What is the administrative fine applied for 2024 in the event a person resists screening or a manual search at security checkpoints despite being warned?

95296.text: For which vehicles are vehicle entry permits issued?
options: Only for vehicles with an operational need
For all vehicles arriving at the airport
Only for vehicles belonging to public institutions
Only for vehicles belonging to airline companies

95297.text: As good practice, what is the recommended maximum validity period for vehicle entry authorisations?

95298.text: In Turkey, which documents must be carried and verified for vehicles entering security restricted areas?
options: Apron plate and vehicle identification card

95299.text: Which of the following is not one of the security checkpoints at airports?

95300.text: Under Annex 17, when must non-passengers and the items they carry be screened?
options: Before they enter security restricted areas
When they exit security restricted areas
Only at the end of the shift

95301.text: Which of the following is correct regarding the method to be used when screening non-passengers?
options: It must be carried out using a method capable of detecting the presence or trace of explosives
A visual check alone is sufficient
Only a metal detector should be used
Only identity verification should be carried out
Only camera recording should be taken

95302.text: When the explosive detection method is applied as an additional method, how must the selection process be carried out?

95303.text: In Turkey, which of the following is correct regarding the screening exemption granted to armed law enforcement officers on duty at the airport?
options: The exemption covers only the items they carry in connection with their duties, and the checking of their entry passes continues
The exemption covers all their personal belongings and entry pass checking is not carried out either
The exemption is also valid outside working hours
The exemption also exempts them from access control
No separate registration procedure is required for the exemption

95304.text: Which of the following is not one of the minimum security measures that must be applied to aircraft under ICAO Annex 17?
options: Reporting the aircraft's commercial performance after the flight
Subjecting aircraft to a security search or security check before the flight
Checking items left behind by disembarking passengers on transit flights
Protecting the cockpit entrance from unauthorised persons during flight

95305.text: What stages does the obligation of airport personnel to observe passengers and other persons cover?
options: Every stage from the airport entry point to boarding the aircraft

95306.text: What is the obligation of staff holding an airport entry pass regarding persons without a pass?
options: To report persons without a pass to the security units or the competent authorities
To escort persons without a pass to the exit
To question and record the identity of persons without a pass
To issue a temporary pass to persons without a pass

95307.text: Which of the following can be given as an example of a suspicious event?
options: Sighting a suspicious or unattended package
An aircraft being taken in for maintenance

95308.text: According to Annex 17 of the Chicago Convention, which reporting system must every member state establish?
options: A publicly accessible event reporting system
A system that accepts only written applications
A closed system accessible only to the competent authority
A system only for airline companies

95309.text: By what means can events assessed as being contrary to the rules at aviation facilities be reported?
options: In writing, verbally, or by e-mail, and through the reporting sections on organisations' websites

95310.text: When reporting an event, how should the stages of the event be ordered?

95311.text: Which of the following is not among the points to be observed when reporting an event?
options: Adding personal comments and speculation to the report
The statements being legible, clear and meaningful
Stating the identities of the victim, suspect and witnesses
Clearly writing when, how and from whom the information was obtained

95312.text: What is the term for the totality of security-related norms, values, attitudes and assumptions reflected by the actions and behaviour of all units and personnel in an organisation's daily operations?

95313.text: Who is responsible for aviation security?
options: Everyone, from the bottom to the top

95314.text: Which of the following is not an indicator of a weak security culture?
options: Event reporting channels being open, known and trusted
Security being thought of as the responsibility of the security unit alone
Information or concerns about violations being concealed
Adopting a reactive rather than proactive approach to security and risk management
Security being seen as a burden for the organisation

95315.text: In a weak security culture, which approach is adopted in security and risk management?
options: A reactive approach instead of a proactive one
A proactive approach instead of a reactive one

95316.text: The emergence of an effective security culture is directly related to which of the following?
options: Security being accepted as a core value rather than as an obligation or a burdensome task
Increasing the number of security personnel

95317.text: Which of the following is correct regarding leadership in security culture?
options: Leaders' decisions greatly influence the organisational security culture
Leaders have limited influence on organisational culture
Security culture is determined only by the behaviour of lower-level staff
Only leaders' budget decisions affect security
Security culture develops independently of leadership

95318.text: Among the practical steps that must be taken to build a positive security culture, what should be done regarding reports notifying suspicious behaviour or negligence?
options: A framework must be established that provides protection for the reports and their sources
The reports must be shared with the public
The identities of report submitters must be announced to all personnel
The reports should be evaluated only at the end of the year
Reporting should be limited to managers only
